what: How much of a real qd-mutate corpus survives rung 0's byte context window, by width. to_decision keeps the TAIL of the post-mutation file and raises SpanOutsideWindow when the gold span falls in the dropped head, so the window decides how much corpus is usable at all.
why: docs/lappi.md calls capacity 'the first thing to raise if rung 0 underperforms'. This is the prior question -- whether there is enough corpus to underperform on. At ByteDeciderConfig's default of 1024, 91% of this corpus is refused, so a run at that width measures its truncation.
clean_share_note: clean is 1.7% of EXAMPLES although --clean-permille defaults to 200 (20%). The flag is per POOL RECORD, and a clean record yields one example while a mutated record yields many, so the example-level rate is an order of magnitude below the record-level setting. 'The model must be able to say this change is fine' is being taught on 1.7% of the corpus.
